title: Nilpotent finite-stage devissage of the cyclic restriction comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. On the coherent profinite site in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention], put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$, $u(k)=k$, and $\tau=u(1)=1$. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with condensed $H$-actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $H$-invariants taken in the full action category. Write
$$c_N=(\lambda_N^1)^{-1}\beta_N^1:R\Gamma_H(N[0])\longrightarrow Q[N\xrightarrow{\tau-1}N]$$
for the invariant-normalized cyclic restriction comparison of [lem-sfb-relative-cyclic-restriction-model], with residual group trivial and cyclic degrees $0,1$.

Assume that $c_A$ for the trivial $H$-module $A$ is an isomorphism. For every finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$, every integer $e\geq1$, and every $E$-linear $D_W:W\to W$ with $D_W^e=0$, give $W$ the action $t\cdot w=\sum_{j=0}^{e-1}t^jD_W^jw/j!$ and put $M(W)(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E W)$ with its finite-dimensional product norm topology and induced action. Then $c_{M(W)}$ is an isomorphism.

More precisely, with $W_0=\ker D_W$ and $\overline W=W/W_0$ carrying the induced nilpotent operator, inclusion and quotient induce a short exact sequence of internal $H$-modules
$$0\longrightarrow M(W_0)\longrightarrow M(W)\longrightarrow M(\overline W)\longrightarrow0.$$
Its underlying sequence of section modules has a splitting natural in every profinite parameter $S$, induced by a continuous $E$-linear complement of $W_0$; no equivariant splitting is claimed. The action on $W_0$ is trivial; if $W\ne0$ then $W_0\ne0$ and $\dim_E\overline W<\dim_E W$.

Let $D_F=1\otimes D_W$ and $U_e(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{e}X^{j-1}/j!$. As endomorphisms of $F\otimes_E W$ one has $\exp(D_F)-1=D_FU_e(D_F)$, and $U_e(D_F)$ is invertible and commutes with $D_F$. As subobjects with their common inclusion into $M(W)$,
$$M(W)^H=\ker(\tau-1)=\ker C(-,D_F).$$
Fixed sections here mean fixed after every profinite base change and by every continuously varying $t$. This includes $W=0$ and $D_W=0$ and imposes no bound uniform over different choices of $W,D_W,e$.

proof.text: Write $P_D(t)=\sum_{j<e}t^jD_W^j/j!$. For $r<e$, the coefficient of $D_W^r$ in $P_D(s)P_D(t)$ is $\sum_{i+j=r}s^it^j/(i!j!)=(s+t)^r/r!$; terms of degree at least $e$ vanish. Hence $P_D(s)P_D(t)=P_D(s+t)$, $P_D(0)=1$ and $P_D(-t)=P_D(t)^{-1}$. In coordinates the action is a finite polynomial in $t$ and the vector coordinates, so is jointly continuous; the map $\mathbf Z_\ell\to E$ is continuous. The same coordinate argument works over the possibly noncomplete field $F$. Apply the continuous-section realization to obtain the specified internal action on $M(W)$; all formulas commute with precomposition in the profinite parameter.

proof.text: Set $W_0=\ker D_W$. Each polynomial $P_D(t)$ restricts to the identity on $W_0$ and induces $P_{\overline D}(t)$ on $\overline W=W/W_0$, where $\overline D^e=0$. Apply the continuous-section exact-triangle statement with $\Pi=H$, $V=W$ and $U=W_0$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and this stability. It gives exactly the asserted short exact sequence, a splitting natural in every profinite $S$ after forgetting the action, and the distinguished triangle of its degree-zero complexes. Concretely, choose lifts of a basis of $\overline W$ and their span $L$; $W=W_0\oplus L$. The resulting continuous $E$-linear section extends to an $F$-linear matrix on finite products of $F$ and then acts on sections by postcomposition. This is the claimed complement splitting, without any equivariance assertion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct images; agent-written finite-stage nilpotent extension argument below the analytic comparison. This auxiliary statement is not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: If $W\ne0$, take $w\ne0$ and the least $r\ge1$ for which $D_W^rw=0$; it exists since $D_W^e=0$. Then $D_W^{r-1}w$ is a nonzero vector of $W_0$. Extend a basis of $W_0$ to a basis of $W$; the added basis vectors project to a basis of $\overline W$. Thus $\dim_E\overline W=\dim_EW-\dim_EW_0<\dim_EW$. This also verifies termination of the induction below.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct images; agent-written finite-stage nilpotent extension argument below the analytic comparison. This auxiliary statement is not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Put $D=D_F$. Expanding the finite sums gives $DU_e(D)=\sum_{j=1}^eD^j/j!=\exp(D)-1$, since $D^e=0$. Write $B=U_e(D)-1=DV(D)$ for a polynomial $V$ (with $V=0$ if $e=1$). Polynomial expressions in $D$ commute, and $B^e=D^eV(D)^e=0$. Consequently $U_e(D)^{-1}=\sum_{k=0}^{e-1}(-B)^k$: multiplying on either side leaves $1-(-B)^e=1$. Both $U_e(D)$ and this inverse commute with $D$. Therefore $(\tau-1)x=DU_e(D)x=U_e(D)Dx=0$ if and only if $Dx=0$. These identities hold on every section module by pointwise application.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct images; agent-written finite-stage nilpotent extension argument below the analytic comparison. This auxiliary statement is not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: By the definition of fixed sections, an $H$-fixed section is fixed by the constant parameter $\tau=1$, hence belongs to $\ker(\tau-1)$ and, by step 4, to $\ker C(-,D_F)$. Conversely, if $D_Fm=0$ on a profinite $S$, then after any $f:T\to S$ we still have $D_F(f^*m)=0$. For any continuous $t:T\to H$, every positive-degree term of $P_D(t)(f^*m)$ vanishes pointwise, so $t\cdot f^*m=f^*m$. This is the full internal fixed-section condition, including varying parameters. All three subobjects thus have the same sections and the same inclusion into $M(W)$, proving the stated equality of subobjects.

proof.text: For a trivial $H$-representation $W$ of dimension $d$, choose a basis. It gives $M(W)\cong A^{\oplus d}$ as action modules, by the coordinate homeomorphism $F\otimes_EW\cong F^d$: by the continuous-section realization this equivariant linear homeomorphism acts by postcomposition, and $C(S,F^d)=C(S,F)^d$ is the section module of the biproduct. The derived invariants functor is additive, and the cyclic comparison is natural between triangulated, hence additive, functors. Under the finite biproduct identifications, naturality for each summand injection and projection identifies $c_{A^{\oplus d}}$ with the diagonal matrix having $d$ entries $c_A$: off-diagonal entries are zero and diagonal entries equal $c_A$. Its inverse is the diagonal matrix of inverses. For $d=0$ this is the unique map between zero objects. Thus the assumption on $c_A$ proves the comparison for every trivial finite-dimensional representation, including $W_0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct images; agent-written finite-stage nilpotent extension argument below the analytic comparison. This auxiliary statement is not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Prove the comparison assertion by strong induction on $n=\dim_EW$, simultaneously for every $e\ge1$ and every $D_W$ with $D_W^e=0$. The case $n=0$ is step 6. If $n>0$, step 3 makes the quotient smaller, so the induction hypothesis gives $c_{M(\overline W)}$ invertible; step 6 gives $c_{M(W_0)}$ invertible. Since $\lambda^1$ is a natural isomorphism, $c_N=(\lambda_N^1)^{-1}\beta_N^1$ is invertible if and only if $\beta_N^1$ is; no shift compatibility of $\lambda^1$ is used. With $G=1$ the relative cyclic model identifies $\beta^1$ with the canonical derived restriction $b_u$ along $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$. The continuous-section exact-triangle statement, applied with $\Pi=H$, this $u$ and the triangle $M(W_0)[0]\to M(W)[0]\to M(\overline W)[0]\to M(W_0)[1]$ of step 2, gives a morphism from the distinguished $R\Gamma_H$-image to the distinguished $R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}D(\operatorname{Res}_u)$-image with components $b_u(M(W_0)),b_u(M(W)),b_u(M(\overline W))$, including the square on the connecting arrow. The outer components are invertible, so the triangle two-out-of-three lemma makes $b_u(M(W))=\beta^1_{M(W)}$, hence $c_{M(W)}$, invertible. This completes the induction. Only the current finite $e$ was used, so no uniform nilpotence bound is introduced.
